_about: Feature questions for medium-risk packages (packages.csv 'feature' column). Only asked when the TV has at least one matching package. 'recommend' is what the wizard suggests; 'unsure' is what happens if the user is not sure. 'off' = switch those packages off, 'keep' = leave them alone.

questions.ask: Do you use your TV brand's own extras on the home screen: free channels, content tabs, sponsored rows, the brand's app store?
questions.help: These are the ads and 'recommended for you' rows. Netflix, YouTube and your other apps are not affected.

questions.ask: Do you watch channels through an antenna, satellite dish or cable plugged straight into the TV (not through an HDMI box)?
questions.help: Say Yes if you ever use the TV's built-in channels. HDMI inputs keep working either way.

questions.ask: Do you ever cast from an iPhone, iPad or Mac (AirPlay)?
questions.help: On our test TV the AirPlay service was stuck using a whole CPU core while nobody was casting.

questions.ask: Do you use Chromecast, the Cast button in YouTube, Netflix and other phone apps?
questions.help: Almost everyone does. Only say No if you are sure.

questions.ask: Do you mirror an Android phone or PC screen to the TV (Miracast, the brand's cast app, DLNA)?
questions.help: This is screen mirroring, not Chromecast.

questions.ask: Do you talk to Alexa through this TV?
questions.help: Google Assistant and the voice button on the remote are never touched.

questions.ask: Do you want to keep the photo/art screensaver (Ambient mode)?
questions.help: It can use about 100 MB of memory. Without it, a TV left idle switches off when the screensaver would have started (10 minutes on the test TV); docs/08 shows how to make that longer.

questions.ask: Do you play videos, music or photos from a USB stick with the TV's built-in player?
questions.help: Apps like VLC can do this instead.

questions.ask: Do you use the TV brand's phone app or smart-home features with this TV?
questions.help: For example Sony BRAVIA Connect or Haier hOn. Google Home is not affected.
